stories.title: LeBron 76ers Big 4 Is Official — No Press Conference, Just Basketball

x_posts.label: Post 1-1
x_posts.text: LeBron hasn't held an introductory press conference since Miami in 2010. Not in LA. Not in Philly. The Big 4 is assembled — Brown, Embiid, Maxey, LeBron — and that's announcement enough. #HoopHeroes #76ers

x_posts.label: Post 1-2
x_posts.text: Rich Paul said Tyrese Maxey was a PRIMARY reason LeBron chose Philly. Brown. Embiid. Maxey. LeBron. Pennsylvania has already declared "LeBron James Day." The 76ers are built to win NOW. #HoopHeroes #76ers

facebook.long_form:
The Philadelphia 76ers' Big 4 is officially assembled — and LeBron James isn't throwing a party about it.

Per ESPN's Brian Windhorst, there will be no introductory press conference in Philadelphia. That's consistent with LeBron's history: he didn't hold one when he joined Miami in 2010, and he didn't hold one when he signed with the Lakers in 2018. The player who changed the game never changes his formula when it comes to showing up for work.

The roster itself is everything the hype suggested. LeBron signed a 2-year, $8 million deal — the veteran's minimum — and the 76ers completed a trade to bring Jaylen Brown from Boston (sending Paul George, two first-round picks, and two second-round picks). The projected starting lineup: Tyrese Maxey, VJ Edgecombe, Jaylen Brown, LeBron James, and Joel Embiid. That is four players who have combined for more All-Star appearances than most franchises see in a decade.

Rich Paul, LeBron's agent, has said that Tyrese Maxey was a primary reason his client chose Philadelphia over the other finalists. LeBron watched Maxey develop into one of the game's best young guards and decided he wanted to be a part of that story. Pennsylvania officially declared "LeBron James Day" on July 24.

No press conference needed. The Big 4 is here, and the city already knows.
facebook.image_caption: No intro press conference. No announcement party. Just four of the best players in basketball assembling in Philadelphia. The LeBron era in Philly has begun — quietly, confidently, and with championship intent.

stories.title: Ja Morant Traded to Portland Trail Blazers — Grizzlies Get Jerami Grant and Kris Murray

x_posts.label: Post 2-1
x_posts.text: TRADE: Ja Morant is headed to Portland. Memphis ships their star to the Trail Blazers for Jerami Grant, Kris Murray, and $1M cash. No picks. Fresh start alongside Deni Avdija and Dame Lillard. #HoopHeroes #TrailBlazers

x_posts.label: Post 2-2
x_posts.text: Morant played just 79 games across THREE seasons — injuries, suspensions, and questions. Portland is betting he can be great again. Avdija. Lillard. Now Morant. The West just got more interesting. #HoopHeroes #TrailBlazers

facebook.long_form:
Ja Morant is heading to Portland — and the Trail Blazers are betting on a talent that has spent years being buried by injuries and poor decisions.

Memphis traded the 26-year-old point guard to Portland in exchange for Jerami Grant, Kris Murray, and $1 million in cash. No draft picks changed hands. From the Grizzlies' perspective, it's a sensible transaction: they shed a player who has appeared in just 79 games over the past three seasons — a stretch defined by suspensions and time lost — and receive two useful rotation players without surrendering future assets.

For Portland, it's an entirely different calculation. The Trail Blazers already brought Damian Lillard back on a three-year deal after Milwaukee waived him. They have Deni Avdija, who emerged as one of the game's most exciting young wings last season. Now they add Morant, who — when healthy and focused — is one of the most electrifying guards in the NBA.

New Portland head coach Micah Nori, formerly an assistant with the Minnesota Timberwolves, will be tasked with harnessing all of that talent and turning it into something coherent. This is a team worth watching in 2026-27.

For Morant, the question is simpler than any roster analysis: Can he stay on the floor and rediscover the player who once looked like the face of a generation? Portland is about to find out.
facebook.image_caption: Fresh start. New city. Ja Morant lands in Portland alongside Damian Lillard and Deni Avdija. The Trail Blazers are betting big on potential — and they might just be right.

stories.title: Kawhi Leonard Investigation — NBA Reviewing Findings, Ruling Imminent

x_posts.label: Post 3-1
x_posts.text: UPDATE: The NBA's outside law firm has FINISHED its fact-finding in the Kawhi Leonard investigation. The league is now reviewing. A ruling is coming — but CBA arbitration rules mean it still takes time. Toronto is stuck. #HoopHeroes #Raptors

x_posts.label: Post 3-2
x_posts.text: The Kawhi Leonard investigation: nearly a year in the making. The trade to Toronto is STILL frozen. Adam Silver has said it must resolve before the 2026-27 season. The Raptors can't plan until this ends. #HoopHeroes #Raptors

facebook.long_form:
The Kawhi Leonard investigation is approaching its moment of resolution — but in the NBA, "imminent" comes with fine print.

The independent law firm hired by the league has completed its fact-finding phase. The NBA is now internally reviewing those findings before determining whether Leonard, the Los Angeles Clippers, or owner Steve Ballmer face any discipline. Commissioner Adam Silver has been clear: this probe must conclude before the 2026-27 season begins.

At the center of the investigation is a $28 million endorsement deal between Leonard and Aspiration Fund Adviser LLC — the financial services firm that has since filed for bankruptcy. The question is whether that deal, and potentially additional personal expense arrangements, violated NBA cap rules. If the league finds wrongdoing, potential penalties include voiding the contract or a fine of up to $350,000. But any proposed punishment must go through an assistant arbitrator under the collective bargaining agreement, and the NBPA retains the right to appeal.

That process is why "imminent" doesn't mean "this week." There are steps.

What is certain: the pending trade that would send Kawhi Leonard to the Toronto Raptors — in exchange for Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick, and draft picks — remains completely frozen until the investigation concludes. Toronto cannot build its roster. The Clippers cannot complete their rebuild. The clock is ticking toward Silver's deadline.
facebook.image_caption: The NBA's outside law firm has finished its fact-finding. The league is reviewing. The Kawhi Leonard trade to Toronto is still frozen — and the whole league is waiting.

stories.title: Bulls Offer DeRozan $80M Over 2 Years — Deal Not Yet Official

x_posts.label: Post 4
x_posts.text: The Kings waived DeMar DeRozan. Now the Chicago Bulls have reportedly offered him 2 years and $80M to return. No confirmed deal yet — but a 6x All-Star going back to where his renaissance started would be a story. #HoopHeroes #Bulls

facebook.long_form:
The Sacramento Kings waived DeMar DeRozan this week. What happens next could define the Chicago Bulls' direction for the next two years.

According to Yahoo Sports, the Bulls have offered DeRozan a 2-year deal worth approximately $40 million per season — an $80 million commitment for a player who turns 37 next winter. The six-time All-Star averaged 18.4 points on nearly 50 percent shooting in Sacramento last season and still has game. He has also previously expressed a desire to return to Chicago, where his career experienced a full renaissance during his three seasons with the Bulls from 2021 to 2024.

The tension here is real. The Bulls spent the better part of this offseason talking about embracing a youth rebuild. They hired Tiago Splitter as their new head coach. They have young pieces in place. Signing DeRozan at $40 million a year runs counter to that stated philosophy.

As of July 28, no deal has been confirmed. This is a reported offer, not a signed contract. The situation is live.

If it happens, DeRozan returns to the city that redefined him. If it falls through, the Bulls stay on their rebuild path — and DeRozan finds another home.
facebook.image_caption: The Chicago Bulls reportedly offered DeMar DeRozan 2 years and $80M. The 6x All-Star has previously said he wants to go back. No deal confirmed yet — but this story is very much alive.

stories.title: Six New NBA Head Coaches for 2026-27 — The Biggest Coaching Overhaul in Years

x_posts.label: Post 5
x_posts.text: Six new head coaches entering 2026-27 — that's one-fifth of the NBA. Dusty May left an NCAA title at Michigan to coach Cooper Flagg in Dallas. Taylor Jenkins gets a second shot in Milwaukee. Tiago Splitter takes Chicago. #HoopHeroes

facebook.long_form:
One-fifth of the NBA enters the 2026-27 season with a new head coach — the largest coaching overhaul the league has seen in years, and each hire carries its own compelling story.

In Dallas, Dusty May walked away from an NCAA championship at Michigan to take on the most high-profile assignment in this year's cycle: coaching No. 1 overall pick Cooper Flagg. May brings a track record of developing offensive systems at the college level, and the Mavericks are betting he can translate that to the NBA stage immediately.

In Milwaukee, Taylor Jenkins returns to head coaching after a season away from the sideline. He inherits a Bucks roster that has been completely reimagined after the Giannis Antetokounmpo trade. Jenkins will need to build chemistry and a new identity quickly.

Tiago Splitter takes over in Chicago, where he'll have the DeRozan situation (if it closes) to navigate alongside a building-block core. Sean Sweeney moves from Spurs Finals assistant to head coach in Orlando, a rapid elevation that speaks to his reputation around the league. Jamahl Mosley transitions from his former post with the Magic to New Orleans, and Micah Nori lands in Portland — immediately tasked with making Ja Morant, Damian Lillard, and Deni Avdija coexist.

The full 2026-27 schedule is expected to drop as soon as next week now that LeBron's landing spot is settled. When it does, these six new coaches will begin charting their paths.
facebook.image_caption: Six new head coaches. Six new systems. Dusty May coaching Cooper Flagg in Dallas. Taylor Jenkins starting over in Milwaukee. The 2026-27 NBA season is already shaping up to be one of the most compelling in years.
